UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE, Plaintiff, v. KATIE HALL, individually; NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN; META PLATFORMS, INC.; and JOHN/JANE DOES 1–6, Defendants. ____________________________________/ | Case No. 1:26-cv-02331

DECLARATION OF MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE IN SUPPORT OF PLAINTIFF’S MOTION UNDER RULE 26(d)(1) FOR PRESENT AUTHORIZATION TO SERVE ONE INTERROGATORY ON NCMEC CONCERNING PLAINTIFF’S FULL LEGAL NAME

I, Marvelle J. Ballentine, declare as follows under 28 U.S.C. § 1746:

1.	I am Marvelle J. Ballentine, the Plaintiff in this action. I make this declaration from personal knowledge and can testify to the facts stated below. Unless a different date is stated, paragraphs 2–17 describe my circumstances as of November 7, 2026.

2.	I reaffirm paragraphs 2–8 of my declaration at ECF No. 31 and paragraphs 2–10 of my declaration at ECF No. 59-2. Those statements remain true within the periods they address.

3.	Before the April 22, 2026 letters, I had never used “Marvelle J. Ballentine” to create, register, identify, maintain, access, or operate any Meta account. I used “Jay Ballentine.” My full legal name appeared in my April 9 materials because it is my legal name and the name in the case captions.

4.	I received the April 22, 2026 letters signed by Katie Hall. The letters led me to seriously contemplate my continued participation in the Florida proceedings identified in those letters.

5.	I have never seen a CyberTipline report. I do not know whether any CyberTipline report, as originally received by NCMEC or submitted by Meta, contains my full legal name.

6.	As of November 7, 2026, the question whether any original CyberTipline report contains “Marvelle J. Ballentine” remained unanswered to me. I had not received the sworn original-report answer requested here from any defendant or its counsel.

7.	On August 13, 2026, I asked counsel for NCMEC and Hall whether the identifiers in the letters appeared in either report as received from the reporting provider. Counsel wrote that “you got exactly what you asked for, using the language you provided.” That response did not answer whether my full legal name appeared in an original report.

8.	Approximately two years before November 7, 2026, I was refused legal services. I understood the refusal to be attributable, at least in part, to the child-sexual-exploitation designation associated with my Meta account.

9.	That refusal occurred before NCMEC’s April 22, 2026 letters. I reported my difficulty obtaining representation in my September 9, 2025 complaint in Ballentine v. Meta Platforms, Inc., No. 3:25-cv-07671, in the Northern District of California. Paragraphs 11–12 described attorneys’ refusal to take my case. Declaration Exhibit 1 contains a true and correct copy of the filed cover page and page 3 of that complaint.

10.	I intend to retain counsel to assume responsibility for my pending litigation. I want to devote more of my time and attention to developing Docket Entry and to my family.

11.	My earlier experience makes me reluctant to expose myself to another rejection while the association between my full legal name and CyberTipline reports remains unresolved. The April 22 letters, their presence in the public litigation record, NCMEC’s defense of them as accurate, and Meta’s description of them as “the exact discovery” have added to that concern.

12.	I am actively developing Docket Entry, an AI-assisted litigation technology business. My work includes developing technology, litigation workflows, and the professional and operational foundation of the business.

13.	My concern about the unresolved public association affects my willingness to participate openly in professional networking, business development, technology incubators, accelerator programs, and founder fellowships.

14.	Those activities involve my identity and professional credibility. I am concerned that the public association may arise in inquiries or record searches connected with those activities.

15.	The continuing uncertainty causes me stress and affects my daily work and family responsibilities. It also affects my intended transition from handling the litigation myself to devoting more attention to Docket Entry and my family.

16.	Accurate sworn reporting information would inform my decisions about seeking counsel and participating openly in professional activities. I want to be able to explain what each organization has stated from its own records. I remain unable to answer the identification question raised by the letters.

17.	As of November 7, 2026, I have received no correspondence from NCMEC indicating that either CyberTipline report described in the April 22, 2026 letters was referred to law enforcement, and I have had no contact from any law-enforcement agency concerning the matters addressed in those letters.

18.	On July 31, 2026, I transmitted to NCMEC and to Ms. Hall a written offer to release every claim against them. The offer required no payment and no admission. It required each of them to sit for one deposition and to produce limited documents. I offered to bear the court-reporter and recording costs of the depositions. The offer expired on August 14, 2026. Neither NCMEC nor Ms. Hall accepted it.

19.	[Complete from the actual telephone conference or attempts with counsel for NCMEC and Hall: date, Eastern time, means, participants, request for a call if applicable, and what occurred. Identify the exact Exhibit A question presented and the request for a voluntary answer.]

20.	[Record counsel’s actual position on the question and a voluntary answer; whether NCMEC’s records can be searched by full name; what additional search steps, time, or expense counsel identified; the proposed seven-day response period or another period; any privilege or confidentiality ground; counsel’s positions on the modified-test and good-cause standards; and counsel’s position on Plaintiff’s waiver of oral argument and request for prompt determination on the papers. Describe any point left unresolved. State agreement only when counsel expressed it.]

21.	[Identify and authenticate any new correspondence attached to document the conference or attempts. If none is attached, state: “No new correspondence is attached to this declaration.” Do not attach material not relied on.]

I declare under penalty of perjury that the foregoing is true and correct.

Executed on __________, 2026.

Marvelle J. Ballentine
